newsitem.title: CHINA: China may release dissident politician next week.
newsitem.headline: China may release dissident politician next week.

text.p: China may end months of house arrest for Bao Tong, the most senior official jailed for the 1989 student-led pro-democracy protests, after his family agreed to move from their government residence, relatives said on Thursday.
"We are very happy," one family member said. "We may be reunited with him next week. That is what the authorities have said."

Chinese authorities had insisted that Bao's family move from their government-allocated apartment in a block reserved for high-ranking officials before they would free the former secretary to Communist Party chief Zhao Ziyang from house arrest.
"We plan to move house next week and that was the condition the authorities had set before they would allow Bao Tong to come home," said the family member who declined to be identified.
"He is very happy because he will soon be reunited with his family after all this time," the family member said.
Bao was released from jail in May, 1996 after serving a six-year prison term for his role in the 1989 student demonstrations, and immediately placed under house arrest in the suburbs of Beijing.
